notes: State rows are only the states GE Aerospace itemised in its March 12, 2024 investment release: Alabama (Auburn $54M), Massachusetts (Lynn $30M) and North Carolina (four facilities $46M: Asheville $11M, Durham >$7M, West Jefferson ~$5M, Wilmington $22M). The release says nearly $450M goes to 22 facilities across 14 states but names only these; the other 11 states have no published amount. Greater Cincinnati ($107M) is a metro area spanning Ohio and Kentucky, so it is recorded as a site, not a state row. The release also cites $100M for U.S. suppliers (not by state) and about $100M for international sites in North America, Europe and India (region row, no country split). The March 12, 2025 release (nearly $1B plan) was also read: it itemises sites (e.g. Greater Cincinnati $113M, Muskegon MI $70M, Auburn AL $51M, Huntsville AL $22M, Asheville NC $20M, Durham NC $16M, West Jefferson NC $13M, West Chester OH $14M, Batesville MS $11M, Lafayette IN $5M) but not state totals, so state values would need summing; it was not used, to keep one plan year. The release's 'interactive map' link now shows the 2026 plan and was not used. 10-K: ~53,000 employees, ~28,000 in the U.S. (US country row); manufacturing and service operations at 67 facilities in 22 states and Puerto Rico and 67 facilities in 24 other countries, with no breakdown by state or country.
